# Storyboard: Chapter 10, The Gathering

*Generated by `tools/storyboard.mjs` from `app/story/ch10.js`. Do not edit by hand: change the story file and run `node tools/storyboard.mjs` again.*

## How to read this

Every screen of the game is one comic panel, called a frame. Frames are listed in reading order. Each one has:

- **Shot**: the storyboard, written for an illustrator (camera, who is where, what the moment feels like, where the lettering goes).
- **Scene**: what the game draws today, in plain words: the set, the camera, who is in shot and how, and any effects.
- **Captions**: the narration boxes, read first. **Balloons**: who speaks, in order. **Sound effect**: the big lettering. A line marked *(only if …)* shows only to a reader whose choices match.
- **Then**: what the reader does next (tap Next, choose, type, pick a look, count by twos, or do a Counts lesson).

Where the reader makes a choice, each option’s frames are grouped under a **Branch** heading, and the branches meet again at the frame named after them. `{name}` is the first part of her Clan name (Moon makes Moonpaw), `{petname}` is what her Tall One calls her, and `{they}`/`{them}`/`{their}` become she/her/her or he/him/his. `{Murmur}`/`{murmur}` is the tortoiseshell’s name word: Murmur (Murmurpaw, Murmurchime, murmuring), or Mutter for a reader whose own Clan name is Murmur.

### f001 · panel 1

**Shot.** WIDE, INSIDE THE DEN, EARLY MORNING. The grey apprentice is still asleep in a curl across the den, and our cat sits up in its moss nest blinking; a big ginger head with a torn ear has poked in through the doorway, its whiskers twitching with news. Caption top left; her balloon a happy whisper.

**Scene.** Den: the apprentices’ den under an enormous rosebush, in the morning. Camera: inside the den (`inside`). Cast: the snoring apprentice (curled up, sleepy, in a nest, left, facing right); you (sitting up on the haunches, both forepaws raised, claws out, full of wonder, in the nest, facing right); Tallyheart (peering, happy, in the doorway, facing left). Also: clear weather; Riffle’s lucky stone in her nest, right where she put it (by her nose or under her chin, as she chose); her Case File along the mossy edge of her nest: a piece of bark for each card she holds, overlapping like roof tiles; her secret cards under the moss, a corner showing for each; her piece of glass in its leaf, tucked under the moss beside the corners of bark: the leaf’s tip and one small glint showing. Effects: morning light, washed clean after the storm.

**Captions**

**Balloons**

- **Tallyheart**, whispering: “Big day. Counts this morning. The Moon Ferry at dusk. And tonight, the Gathering.”

**Shot.** WIDE, THE CLEARING, THE TAP PICTURE. The old GroveClan elder turns her sharp eyes on our cat and remembers it from the woods; our cat ducks its head, nose low. In play its nose glows softly; one tap dips its head very politely and turns the page. Her balloon pleased.

**Scene.** Island: Gathering Island, a round island in the river, at night under the full moon, high and bright silver, never dark (one great tree in the middle, very old and wide-crowned, never named, its huge roots running out across a clearing of short moonlit grass; the three leaders sit on three big roots, never in the branches; the crowd of every Clan sits round the clearing; the shore pebbles and soft mud; everything silver under the full moon, nothing frightening). Camera: wide: the clearing under the great tree, every Clan: the trunk at the middle back, its three big roots running out, a leader on each; the crowd in a wide ring (CrystalClan at the left, ReedClan’s marsh coats at the right, GroveClan’s dappled coats at the back), the river at the far right edge (`wide`). Cast: the GroveClan elder (a she-cat: a dappled grey-brown coat, the dapples like sun through leaves, a white muzzle, grey hairs at her ears; upright and sharp-eyed, hazel eyes, kind) (sitting, kind, at the back left of the ring, in front of the roots, facing right); Sloshbank, the ReedClan tom (big, heavy and stern, solid brown with darker legs, bigger than Tallyheart; his belly fur clumped wet, always dripping, big muddy paws) (sitting, stern, at the front of the ring, ReedClan’s side at the right, first, facing left); the ReedClan she-cat (sleek, dark grey-brown, a pale belly, calm amber eyes; mud to the elbows) (sitting, at the front of the ring, ReedClan’s side, second, facing left); Tallyheart (sitting, kind, at the front of the ring, CrystalClan’s side at the left, first, facing right); you (crouching, kind, in the middle of the clearing, facing left, the nose is what she taps); Riffle, the otter pup (sitting, happy, at the front of the ring, CrystalClan’s side, second, facing right); the young ReedClan tom (lanky and sandy, big ears, eager; mud to the elbows) (sitting, at the front of the ring, ReedClan’s side, third, facing left). (`coil-diggers`), Patience says two small shapes crossed her mud, carrying something. (`heron-shapes`), Tiny prints in the marsh mud. Much smaller than a cat’s. (`prints-marsh`), Thin brown fur at the Crossing. Not cat. Not otter. Not fox. (`fur`), Four gone every night. (`four-a-night`), Tiny prints in the dug earth behind the pile. (`prints-pile`, a card only some cats hold), The tiny prints run toward the train tracks. (`prints-tracks`, a card only some cats hold), Squall says two skinny shapes carry something to the tracks. (`squall-shapes`, a card only some cats hold), Puddle says clever little paws picked up mice on the storm night. (`puddle-paws`, a card only some cats hold), Hail says two skinny shapes cross her field every night, toward the tracks. (`hail-shapes`, a card only some cats hold), My count: twenty-four gone in six nights. A dragon would take sixty. (`my-count`, a card only some cats hold). Any other card: “Hmm. ## The Case File’s cards

A piece of bark for each thing she finds out: one picture scratched in, one line, and a mark in a corner (an eye for what she saw herself, an ear for what she was only told). Each goes into her Case File at the panel that gives it, in this order:

| Card | Mark | Its line | Given at | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## The book page

Title: *{name}paw’s First Moon*. This chapter’s page, under “Chapter 10: The Gathering”. Lines shown when their condition matches the reader’s choices:

- (always) On the morning of the Gathering, Tallyheart taught {name}paw {their} tenth Count, clutches of seven: the sevens.
- (always) At dusk the otters’ Moon Ferry carried CrystalClan upriver under the full moon, and Tallyheart ran the Counts to steady everyone’s nerves.
- (if ch10Puddle is true) Under the Moon Ferry, {name}paw found Puddle, Sprinkle’s brother with the enormous feet, who saw clever little paws picking up mice on the storm night.
- (always) On Gathering Island, Reynard told every Clan his story, and {name}paw answered it, card by card, out loud.
- (always) Snip and Snatch blamed each other and told everything, and every Clan, standing together, sent the fox and the weasels away past the last post.
- (always) Then the Mistscales came in the mist for their clutch, and Sprinkle’s wing held: she flew to her Mama.
- (if foundSquall is true and foundPuddle is true and foundWisp is true and foundSleet is true and foundHail is true and foundMizzle is true) The eldest Mistscale bowed low to {name}paw, the cat who found all seven.
- (always) Sprinkle pressed her grey pebble into {name}paw’s paws, and under the full moon it flashed blue and green: a mist stone.
- (always) In front of every Clan, Glintstar said that {name}paw belongs to CrystalClan, and Tallyheart said {their} warrior name is coming, with this moon in it.
- (always) At bedtime there were ten claw marks on the tree, and a mist stone on the moss.
- (no dream typed) {name}paw’s dream, the night of the Gathering, stayed a secret.
